0.long_answer: Diabetic retinopathy is a condition in which prolonged high blood sugar from diabetes damages the blood vessels in the retina, leading to microaneurysms, hemorrhages, and other vascular abnormalities. These microaneurysms are small bulges in the blood vessel walls and represent one of the early signs of the disease. As diabetic retinopathy progresses, the risk of significant vision impairment or blindness increases, making it one of the leading causes of blindness, particularly among working-age adults.
